title: Like a lotus in water
hook: the God-conscious one lives untouched, like a lotus in water

segments.voice: Yesterday, the brahm giaanee: true in mind, true in speech, seeing the One in all. Your line was the god-conscious one. Today, the portrait gets its first picture. Day four hundred sixty-seven.

If you've ever seen a lotus up close, you'll know the trick. It grows from the mud at the bottom of a pond. Its stem rises through murky water. And then the leaf and the flower open on the surface, and if you splash water on them, it beads up and rolls right off. The leaf is in the water its whole life, and it doesn't get wet. The Guru Granth Sahib returns to this flower more than once. Today it opens the first stanza of the brahm giaanee's portrait.
screen: `ROOTED IN MUD.` → `RISING THROUGH MURKY WATER.` → `THE WATER BEADS AND ROLLS OFF.`

segments.voice: The first line: brahm giaanee sadaa nirlep. The God-conscious one is always nirlep, untouched, unstained. Lep is a coating, a smear, something that sticks to you. Nir means without. So: nothing sticks. Then the picture: jaise jal meh kamal alep. Just as the lotus in water stays unstained. Kamal is the lotus. Notice what the picture doesn't say. It doesn't say the lotus leaves the pond. It doesn't float off to some clean place. It lives in the water, all its life. That matters in Sikh teaching, which asks people to live in the world, work, marry, raise children, pay bills, and not run away to the forest. Guru Nanak used the same image in the Sidh Gosht, when yogis asked how one crosses the ocean of the world: like a lotus in water, untouched, and like a duck swimming in a stream, whose feathers stay dry. The brahm giaanee is in the mess. The mess just doesn't stick. The very next line adds a second picture: the God-conscious one is free of fault, like the sun that dries up everything. The sun shines on clean and dirty places alike, and it doesn't get dirty doing it. Two pictures, one idea. You can be fully in the middle of things, the office, the family argument, the crowded train, and still not be stained by them. Untouched doesn't mean unfeeling. It means the anger in the room doesn't become your anger.
screen: `NIRLEP: NOTHING STICKS.` · `KAMAL: THE LOTUS STAYS IN THE POND.` · `GURU NANAK: THE LOTUS AND THE DUCK.` · `THE SUN, UNSTAINED BY WHAT IT DRIES.` · then, large: `UNTOUCHED, LIKE THE LOTUS.`

segments.voice: The practice: stay calm in one mess. First, rehearse it now. Think of a small mess waiting for you today: an inbox, a difficult relative, a sink full of dishes. Picture yourself in the middle of it. Then picture the lotus leaf, and the water beading up and rolling off. Breathe in: I'm in the water. Breathe out: it rolls off. You're not pretending the mess isn't there. You're just not letting it soak in. Then, later today, try it for real, once. The bell holds the time.
Like a lotus in water. Jaise jal meh kamal alep: the God-conscious one lives in the world, untouched, like the lotus in the pond.
screen: `LIKE A LOTUS IN WATER — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: untouched, like the lotus. In one mess today, stay in it, do your part, and let what isn't yours roll off. Day four hundred sixty-seven.

howItsDone: Sikhs often use the lotus in water, from Sukhmani Sahib and Guru Nanak's Sidh Gosht, to describe living as a householder in the world without being stained by it.

original.note: Gurmukhi: kamal, the lotus; rooted in mud, untouched by the water it lives in.

trapdoor: what you thought: being untouched means staying away from the mess.
what it means: the lotus lives in the pond all its life and stays dry.
what a scholar hears: nirlep (nir- 'without' + lep 'coating'); the lotus image recurs in Gurbani, notably in Guru Nanak's Sidh Gosht (Ang 938), as the model of the householder's detachment.

sources.work: Guru Granth Sahib (Guru Arjan, Gauri Sukhmani)

notes: Editor review (2026-10-01): cut the unsourced 'poets across India have loved this flower for thousands of years'; the Sidh Gosht reference now says the yogis asked how to cross the world-ocean.

Lines paraphrased: brahm giaanee sadaa nirlep / jaise jal meh kamal alep / brahm giaanee sadaa nirdokh / jaise soor sarab kau sokh. Confirm glosses (nirdokh as free of fault; the sun 'dries up everything').
Sidh Gosht lotus-and-duck lines (jaise jal meh kamal niraalam, murgaaee nai saane) placed at Ang 938, pauri 5; confirm.
Lotus leaf shedding water (beading) is botanical fact; fine.
